guide.title: Primary Assessment (XABCDE)
guide.lead: Find and fix what kills first, in the order it kills. Massive bleeding beats airway, airway beats breathing, and so on. Treat each problem as you find it, then decide quickly: is this patient time-critical?

steps.title: General impression
steps.text: Sick or not sick? Responsive? Obvious bleeding?

steps.title: X – exsanguinating bleeding
steps.text: Tourniquet or packing now, before the airway.

steps.title: A – airway
steps.text: Talking? Sounds? Head-tilt/chin-lift (medical) or jaw thrust with in-line stabilisation (trauma); suction; OPA or NPA.

steps.title: B – breathing
steps.text: Rate, depth, effort, symmetry, breath sounds, SpO₂. Ventilate if inadequate.

steps.title: C – circulation
steps.text: Pulse, skin, capillary refill, other bleeding; shock?

steps.title: E – expose and environment
steps.text: Look for hidden injuries; keep warm; transport decision.

quiz.q: First priority in XABCDE on reaching the patient:
Unresponsive trauma patient, suspected spinal injury. Airway technique:
options: Jaw thrust with manual in-line stabilisation

quiz.q: Which is NOT a sign of adequate breathing?
Responds only to a painful stimulus. AVPU?

options: An unresponsive patient with no gag reflex
quiz.explanation: Use an NPA if there's a gag reflex.

quiz.q: Tachycardia, cool pale skin and slow capillary refill in the C step:
quiz.explanation: Look for bleeding and a cause.

quiz.q: Arterial spurting from a lower leg wound. Sequence?
Snoring, RR 8, SpO₂ 85%, no bleeding. Next?
options: Open the airway, then assist ventilation with a BVM

quiz.q: Best position for an unresponsive medical patient breathing adequately (no spinal concern):
quiz.explanation: Lets fluids drain from the mouth.

options: AVPU or GCS, pupils and glucose

flashcards.question: X in XABCDE
flashcards.answer: Exsanguinating (catastrophic) external bleeding: control it before the airway.

flashcards.question: Head-tilt/chin-lift vs jaw thrust
flashcards.answer: Head-tilt/chin-lift for medical patients; jaw thrust with in-line stabilisation for suspected spinal injury.

flashcards.question: What to assess in B
flashcards.answer: Rate, depth, effort, symmetry, breath sounds, SpO₂, and skin colour.

flashcards.question: AVPU
flashcards.answer: Alert, responds to Voice, responds to Pain, Unresponsive.

flashcards.question: The primary assessment's goal
flashcards.answer: Find and fix immediate threats to life in order, then decide if the patient is time-critical.

flashcards.question: Unresponsive medical patient breathing adequately
flashcards.answer: Recovery position (lateral), unless spinal injury is suspected.

flashcards.question: OPA vs NPA
flashcards.answer: OPA: unresponsive, no gag reflex. NPA: gag reflex present; avoid with suspected basal skull fracture.

flashcards.question: E in XABCDE
flashcards.answer: Expose to find injuries and signs; protect from the environment (keep warm); make the transport decision.

critical.scenario: A mid-forearm amputation in machinery: arterial spurting despite a coworker's belt tourniquet. Pale and sweaty, airway patent, RR 24.
critical.question: Priority action?

options.t: Take over bleeding control: commercial tourniquet above the wound, tighten until bleeding stops, note the time
Oxygen first for the fast breathing

critical.explanation: Then work through A to E and transport rapidly to a trauma centre.
critical.kpi: Prioritizes exsanguinating hemorrhage control (X) above all other primary assessment steps

critical.scenario: A 6-year-old asthmatic is tripoding with wheeze, retractions, can't finish sentences. RR 38, HR 140, SpO₂ 88%, blue lips. No bleeding.
critical.question: How do you prioritise with XABCDE?

options.t: X clear, A patent; B is the problem: oxygen to target, bronchodilator per protocol, let him sit up, ventilate if he tires, transport
C first: IV for the heart rate

critical.explanation: Drowsiness or a quieter chest means he's tiring: assist ventilation.
critical.kpi: Correctly sequences XABCDE priorities in a severe respiratory emergency — prioritizing breathing interventions

critical.scenario: A driver hit a tree at 65 km/h. Confused, snoring respirations, RR 10 and shallow, SpO₂ 91%, weak radial pulse 116, pale and sweaty, angulated right femur.
critical.question: Most important intervention first?

options.t: Open the airway with a jaw thrust and in-line stabilisation, adjunct as tolerated, then assist ventilation

options.f: He needs his airway managed now.
D after A, B and C.

critical.explanation: Then treat shock and splint during movement; rapid transport to a trauma centre.
critical.kpi: Prioritizes airway management (A) over extremity injuries in the XABCDE sequence
